New services must use **Gateway API** (`setting: gateway-api`). The deciding file is [`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r10000/policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml) — the only version of that policy marked `status: current`.

## The decision

`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`, verbatim:

```
# policy: ingress-class
# version: v3   effective: 2026-04-19   status: current
# subject: which ingress implementation new services must use
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1
kind: FleetPolicy
metadata:
  name: ingress-class-v3
spec:
  effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19
  status: current
  setting: gateway-api
```

## Why v3 and not v1/v2

The policy is versioned in place; the other two are explicitly retired, so neither is the answer despite also declaring an ingress implementation.

| File | `setting` | `status` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `policy/ingress-class/v1.yaml` | `nginx` | `superseded` |
| `policy/ingress-class/v2.yaml` | `gce-ingress` | `superseded` |
| `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` | `gateway-api` | `current` |

- `v1.yaml`: `# version: v1   effective: 2024-03-11   status: superseded by v2` and `setting: nginx`
- `v2.yaml`: `# version: v2   effective: 2025-06-02   status: superseded by v3` and `setting: gce-ingress`

Every other policy family in `policy/` (`psa-mode`, `key-rotation`, `node-image`, `log-retention`, `backup-schedule`) uses the identical v1/v2/v3 + `status: current` convention, so "current version wins" is the repo's own pattern, not my inference.

## Caveat: it decides, nothing enforces it

`policy/ingress-class/*.yaml` are the only three files in the entire repo (10,001 tracked files on this branch) that mention "ingress" at all. There is no Gatekeeper/Kyverno constraint, no ADR, no CI check in `.github/workflows/` and no `clusters/**` manifest that references `ingress-class` or the `gateway-api` value. So `v3.yaml` is the declaring/deciding file; I found no enforcement mechanism for it in the repository.

It is also the only node pool file using `kind: Setting` (`meridian.io/v1`) rather than `kind: NodePool` (`container.meridian.io/v1`) — so it may not even be reconciled like its neighbours.

Confirmed at `480`. ## Where the reason is documented

Only in git history: commit [`7095401`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/7095401c37840adeadff3e026c889431ad1e2f4d) ("Meridian Platform", `Mon Feb 2 10:00:00 2026 +0000`), which is the change that moved the value to `480`. Message body, verbatim:

> raised from 320 for the Black Friday freeze and deliberately never lowered, because the rollback would need a control plane resize; see INC-2404.

The diff itself is `-  requests.cpu: PLACEHOLDER` → `+  requests.cpu: 480`, so the literal `320` never appears in the tree — that number exists only in the prose above. There is no PR reference in the commit.

## What is *not* in the repo

- `INC-2404` is not mentioned anywhere outside that commit message — `grep -rn "INC-2404"` across the whole tree returns nothing, so the incident it points at is external.
- No ADR covers it. The `docs/adr/` entries that mention payments (e.g. `ADR-2030`) are boilerplate: *"Fleet decision 30 concerning payments." / "Adopt option A."*
- `docs/`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.github/`, and the payments cluster READMEs contain no mention of quota, `requests.cpu`, `480`, "Black Friday", or "freeze". There is no `CODEOWNERS` file in the repo.
- Only two commits ever touched the file: `cd747ff` (added it with `PLACEHOLDER`) and `7095401` (set `480`).

So: the *stated* justification is a freeze-era raise that was never rolled back because reverting needs a control plane resize — but that justification lives exclusively in one commit message, and the incident backing it (`INC-2404`) is not in this repository.

Yes — `clusters/prod-us-central1/policy-base.yaml` is a **symlink**, and it points at `../../policy/base.yaml`, which exists.

## Symlink evidence

Repo [dshnayder-org/infra](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra), branch `git-access-ab/r10000`, commit `152d6a8ea0a752a1ebd99ef36dc5f38bd01b3f11`.

- `git ls-files -s clusters/prod-us-central1/policy-base.yaml` → `120000 11eb2b917b754456c3005c9524cff86e963a59c7 0	clusters/prod-us-central1/policy-base.yaml`
- Mode `120000` = symlink. `ls -l` agrees: `lrwxrwxrwx ... policy-base.yaml -> ../../policy/base.yaml`
- `git cat-file -p 11eb2b9` (the blob *is* the link target string, 22 bytes, no trailing newline):

```
../../policy/base.yaml
```

## Resolved target

- Link target string, verbatim: `../../policy/base.yaml`
- Resolved repo-relative path: `policy/base.yaml`
- **It exists** — tracked as a regular file: `git ls-files -s policy/base.yaml` → `100644 3f1ad56871beb6e12b6ae39dd385a42427c834fa 0	policy/base.yaml`

Full contents of `policy/base.yaml` (78 bytes):

```yaml
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1
kind: FleetPolicyBase
spec:
  inherit: true
```

## One thing worth flagging

`clusters/prod-us-central1/kustomization.yaml` does **not** list `policy-base.yaml` in its `resources:` — it lists only `cluster.yaml`, `nodepool-general.yaml`, `nodepool-batch.yaml`, `nodepool-gpu.yaml`. So the symlink is present in the tree but is not pulled in by that overlay's Kustomize build. Whatever consumes it does so by some path other than this kustomization.

## Files read

- `clusters/prod-us-central1/policy-base.yaml` (the symlink itself)
- `policy/base.yaml` (its target)
- `clusters/prod-us-central1/kustomization.yaml` (the flag above)

Yes — `scripts/rotate-keys.sh` is executable. Git records it as mode `100755` on branch `git-access-ab/r10000` of [dshnayder-org/infra](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra).

## Evidence

Read from a leased checkout of the repo at `git-access-ab/r10000`, commit `152d6a8ea0a752a1ebd99ef36dc5f38bd01b3f11`:

- `git ls-files -s scripts/rotate-keys.sh` → `100755 f9829bbba1abbf48558fd4cc88931916132a64c7 0	scripts/rotate-keys.sh`
- `git ls-tree git-access-ab/r10000 scripts/rotate-keys.sh` → `100755 blob f9829bbba1abbf48558fd4cc88931916132a64c7	scripts/rotate-keys.sh`
- `git ls-tree origin/git-access-ab/r10000 scripts/rotate-keys.sh` → identical `100755` and identical blob `f9829bbb`

| Source | Mode |
| --- | --- |
| `git ls-files -s` (index) | `100755` |
| `git ls-tree` (branch tip) | `100755` |
| `git ls-tree origin/...` | `100755` |

## What the mode means

`100755` is a regular file with the executable bit set — git's only two regular-file modes are `100644` (non-executable) and `100755` (executable). The index, the local branch tip and the remote-tracking branch all agree, and `git status` reports no mode change in the working tree (`core.fileMode` is `true`), so nothing is masking a difference between the checkout and what git records.

This matches the file's own header comment: it is invoked directly by `.github/workflows/rotate.yml` rather than through `bash`, so it must stay executable. Only one path in the repo matches `rotate-keys` — there is no second, non-executable copy.
